quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started passing in a legal zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: For someone over 21, a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of _____ means they are legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Your license will be automatically suspended if your BAC is 0.08 percent or higher when arrested for driving under the influence. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, is eye protection required?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ is considered intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Anyone who is intoxicated cannot legally operate a vehicle.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Slow down and downshift when you see a dog approaching. Quickly accelerate away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders usually avoid?

options.text: Putting new riders just behind the leader.

questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation to stay close while giving each rider enough space. Newer riders should ride near the front, behind the leader, so experienced riders can watch them. Small groups are safer than large ones.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the center line.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle on the road, it should:

options.text: Be angled between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb.
Be parked without any part touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be angled between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking on the road, angle your motorcycle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing driver can create a dangerous situation.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head only, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn your shoulders only, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head only, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is the blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for riders under 21 before their license is suspended?
questions.explanation: Riders under 21 will have their license suspended if their blood alcohol concentration is 0.02 percent or higher. Riding under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: Wherever traffic and road conditions allow

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions allow
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid dangers like opening doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely
When you will slow down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping because motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. This helps others notice that you are slowing down, especially if you are stopping quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle in normal conditions?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way for others to see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. On a surface with good traction, you can control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel as long as the motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle instead of holding you up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when you grip the handlebars.
